svg.title: Hyperspace control model — who may write a parameter
svg.desc: Scene-setters write the base; exactly one performer row writes an offset through Router.modulate; Registry.apply lands base plus offset on the live object once per frame; the render stack only reads. Text twin in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §3.
svg.text: Scene-setters — write the BASE, never prompt, never blocked
panel widgets · key / pad rows (routing.act) · APC40 knobs, faders, buttons
presets, themes, projects (Registry.restore) · mouse, sticks, ↑/↓ (Param.nudge / scale)
R, F1–F8 (app.act)
every path ends in Param.set → _base while a performer holds the param
relative writers read .base, never .value (audit sim 1)
The one performer — writes an OFFSET, one row per target
lane:i · hand:i · ext:i · lfo:i (LANE_SCHEMES)
op push: offset = depth · scale · (u − rest)
op position: offset = clamp(depth · scale · u) − base_norm
Router.modulate → Param.modulate — the only caller in the package
a second row on the target → Owned → Replace / Keep (Bindings edit doors)
Param
base + Σ offsets → effective
Registry.apply(), once per frame, after every source has spoken
a direct object write since last frame is folded into the base first
base
offset
The live object
ViewState · FxState · DreamState · Analyzer · Output · a list slot
put(effective)
Object writers (bypass Param)
ViewState.integrate → ang
camera.reset · Control resets
folded into the base next frame
Readers (never write)
Renderer.draw · Lookback · FxChain
LFO.step (its own fields) · bridge out
see last frame's effective value — the one-frame lag
Chaining, not stacking: LFO knobs and macro.1–8 are Params too, so a performer may own them; a route's scale reads a macro's effective value.
